betterCitation: Anton Chekhov, The Cherry Orchard, Act IV, as the family leaves the house, answering Anya (Trofimov) (trans. Constance Garnett, 1923)
reason: Wording and translator hold; the locator does not. I downloaded the archive.org OCR of the Chatto and Windus volume (imprint: First published April 1923) and it reads ANYA. Good-bye, home! Good-bye to the old life! then TROFIMOV. Welcome to the new life! then the stage direction Trofimov goes out with Anya, Varya looks round the room and goes out slowly. So Garnett’s wording is exactly the proposed line and the speaker is Trofimov. But the source card calls it the last exchange of Act IV, and it is not: after it come Lopahin’s Till the spring, then, the scene of Lyubov and Gaev alone, the offstage voices of Anya and Trofimov, Lyubov’s One last look at the walls, and Firs’s closing speech. A reader sent to the last exchange finds Firs. The evidence locator (before Varya looks round the room and goes out) is right; the card should say that instead.
